answer: During confirmation, each agent must embed a thread of executed transactions into a marshmallow wrapper whose sugar crystals align along a unique slope. This must be validated by peers at the summit, where a 144ms verification lag per wrapper forces graders to check the horizon timing. Each fake identity burns its own wrapper, losing 144ms of unshaved verification time that can’t be bulk-parallelized—the wrapper lattice rejects cloned activations, scaling costs linearly with clones.
